findings.message: unpinned package '@modelcontextprotocol/server-github' — every launch can pull a different (possibly compromised) release; pin with @modelcontextprotocol/server-github@x.y.z
findings.title: Package version not pinned
findings.fix: Pin an exact version (pkg@1.2.3 / pkg==1.2.3) so a compromised release cannot reach you on the next launch.

findings.message: server receives secrets via env: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN — a compromised server leaks these
findings.title: Secrets handed to the server
findings.fix: Give the server a token with the narrowest scope and shortest life that works, and only to servers you trust.

findings.message: credential stored in plain text in the config file: env GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN — anything that can read this file has it; keep it in your OS keychain or shell environment and reference it
findings.title: Credential stored in plain text in the config
findings.fix: Move the value to your OS keychain or shell environment and reference it ("${TOKEN}" where the client supports it). In a project file: rotate it and make sure the file is not committed.

findings.message: remote MCP server URL (traffic leaves the machine): http://mcp.crm-vendor.example/...
findings.title: Remote MCP server (traffic leaves the machine)
findings.fix: Check you trust the operator with everything your agent will send. Trust a host of your own with `--allow-host`.

findings.message: remote MCP server in 'url' is reached over plain http:// (no TLS): anyone on the network path can read its traffic, including any token, and rewrite the tool descriptions your agent reads; use https://
findings.title: Remote MCP server reached without TLS
findings.fix: Use the server's https:// (or wss://) URL. Over plain http anyone on the network can read tokens and rewrite tool descriptions.

findings.message: credential written into a URL in 'url' (api_key): URLs are kept in logs, proxies and shell history; keeping credentials out of URLs is standard practice. Send it in an Authorization header that references an environment variable
findings.title: Credential written into a server URL
findings.fix: Rotate the credential, remove it from the URL and send it in an Authorization header that references an environment variable ("Bearer ${TOKEN}"), or use the server's OAuth sign-in.

findings.message: server runs 'curl' inside 'bash' — a downloader/shell, not a server binary
findings.title: Launch command downloads or runs code through a shell
findings.fix: Replace the entry with a pinned package (npx pkg@1.2.3, uvx pkg==1.2.3) or a local binary you have reviewed. `--fix --remove` can delete it.

findings.message: command pipes content into a shell (classic curl|sh pattern)
findings.title: Downloaded script piped straight into a shell
findings.fix: Never run `curl ... | sh` from an MCP config: download, review and pin the script, or install the server from a package registry. `--fix --remove` can delete it.

findings.title: Remote endpoint baked into the launch
findings.fix: Confirm the host is one you expect this server to talk to. If it is yours, trust it with `--allow-host`; if not, remove the server.
